Never executed (cov_all 0%). Tests connect through SDK().Connect instead, and no test runs `mcp serve`, so the startup log line and stdio serving are unverified.

applyPlan (plan.go:411) sends every failure through it, including 'failed:' after execute and 'not applied:'. The doc saying 'a refused call' undersells this. When the error is itself the audit failure (plan.go:491-493), it re-writes and the message repeats the audit error twice.
Swapping %[1]s and %[2]s (context and cluster) survives. Tool names mentioned in the text are not checked against the registered tools, so a rename would leave stale instructions.

Names are lowercased before matching, so prefixes are lowercased too (L44-47), but patterns are compiled case-sensitive. Verified: the pattern WLM[0-9]+ never matches WLM01 (lowercased to wlm01). The node silently falls through to the catch-all rule and gets wlm01.example.org instead of the hpc domain. The docs mention lowercasing, which only partly mitigates this.

IPv4 passes through only because it contains a dot. An IPv6 literal gets a domain appended. Verified: FQDN("fe80::1") = "fe80::1.example.org", and nodeset accepts fe80::1. So `node fqdn fe80::1` prints a bogus host, and checkSiteHosts sees it as in-domain. BMC refuses IPs explicitly.

If a rule sets both pattern and prefixes, the switch checks only the pattern, and New does not reject the combination. Verified: with the rule {pattern gpu[0-9]+, prefixes [exe]}, FQDN("exe01") falls through to the catch-all rule and returns exe01.example.org. The schema says 'by prefix or by regular expression'.

Nothing outside tests calls it. App.BMCHosts duplicates the loop but prefers the inventory's bmcAddress, a documented safety choice. A future caller of this exported method would skip that preference and send BMC credentials to a derived name.

out.Add parses an expression, not a single name. Verified: Add("a b") succeeds and yields a,b. A domain value containing a space or comma (domains are not validated) would silently turn one node into two hosts, not the 'not a valid host name' error the message implies.

A Result carrying only Object under -o table/wide goes to writeTable(nil), which returns nil with no output. Verified: `clusterctl config view` (config.go:312) at the default -o table prints nothing and exits 0.
The encoder HTML-escapes by default, so a reason like 'temp > 90C' prints as 'temp > 90C'. The JSON is valid but harder for a person to read, and the output guide does not mention it.

The doc says Split is used for group source definitions converted from an older format. Its only callers are shellquote_test.go and cli/tunnel_test.go, and group sources now take argv lists. The doc describes a use that does not exist, and exported production code is kept only for tests.

Every caller (Drain, Resume, AddAccount, SetCoordinators, SetFairShare, AddUser x2, setDefaultAccount) ignores the returned lines, so the doc's 'returns its lines' describes an unused result.

ExitCode <= 0 also catches a truncated result, where the transport sets Err with exit status 0. That result is classed as Transport (3) although the host answered, and the doc names only 'no exit status at all'.
The same wrap-unless-coded pattern is written inline in internal/cli/bmc.go:288-291 and internal/safety/safety.go:113-116.

A '|' inside a value shifts the later columns, and the surplus is dropped without an error. Accounts parses Description and Organization this way, and ValidateText lets --description 'a|b' through. If sacctmgr prints the value verbatim, account list would misreport the organisation and drop coordinators.
The parameter fields shadows the package-level func fields, and the constructor has no doc comment.

sinfo is called without --all, while CheckNodes (L396-398) and bmc.go:365 add it because nodes of hidden partitions are otherwise left out. Nodes that CheckNodes accepted and scontrol changed can then be missing from node list, plan warnings and readBack.
In this package 'NodeSet' also means a slurm.conf NodeSet name (L384, L415), so c.NodeSet(ctx, states) can read as resolving one.
At call sites, refuseAll(ns) reads as refusing the whole set rather than the word ALL.
It checks emptiness and length on the trimmed reason but returns no normalised value. The CLI (slurm.go:145) and MCP (plan.go:106) both trim first, and Drain sends whatever it is given.

A node that sinfo did not return is reported as definitely not in the state. Nodes lacks --all, so a hidden-partition node that CheckNodes accepted (it adds --all for exactly this reason) can be reported as not drained after a partial update.

sinfo %P marks the default partition with '*', so Partition.Name is 'main*' in the JSON and MCP output. That value cannot be passed back as the name filter (--partition main*). Nodes in the same file already uses %R.

Confirmed with a probe: the description 'Physics | Detectors' (accepted by ValidateText, or set directly with sacctmgr) comes back as Description 'Physics ', Organization ' Detectors', Coordinators 'example', and the real coordinators are lost. A newline in a description could add a forged account row.

Cluster's doc notes that one slurmdbd can serve several clusters. Without cluster= or a Cluster field, the same account and user appear once per cluster with different limits, and nothing says which row applies to this cluster.
With no cluster= condition and no Cluster field, a user's associations and default account from every cluster served by the slurmdbd are listed together and cannot be told apart.
Duplicates AccountLimits: both list account associations ('withassoc' vs '--associations'), and AccountLimits already returns Account, User and Fairshare.

Safety depends on the caller calling ValidateName first. Drain validates inside itself; here a new caller passing 'proj[1-100]' would create a hundred accounts.

SetCoordinators(ctx, "proj", []string{"bob"}) leaves alice as a coordinator. The name, and the CLI message 'coordinators of proj set', suggest the list is replaced, while the CLI help says 'Add coordinators'.
'and' at package level reads like an operator; a reader of and(u.associate) must look up what it does.

Swapping values and into still compiles and silently writes into the wrong map. naming.go:40 ignores the return value, and the nil-into branch (67-69) has no caller. The doc comment does not say that into is modified.

Output directories are written over, never cleaned. After a command is renamed, `make docs` or site/build.sh (line 185, in the working tree) leaves the old page in site/content/reference, and Hugo renders it. CI uses a fresh checkout, so only local builds drift.

Account never validated. `clusterctl copy -n exe1 -u 'x:y' f /tmp/` emits "x:y@exe0001...:/tmp/" (probe confirmed); scp splits at the first ':' and targets host "x". The same -u on the real ssh path exits 2, as doc/transport.md promises.
The colon branch, the case the comment leads with, is never executed. Removing it would let a download destination "a:b" be read as a remote host, and every test would still pass.

cmd.Stdout = os.Stderr bypasses the app's streams, so harnesses cannot capture it and parallel progress meters interleave on one terminal. Stderr over DefaultMaxOutput is cut silently, with no Truncated flag as Run sets.

Unlike Client.Run it skips destination() and the guarded length check. A probe showed CLI `exec -u 'x:y'` passing against the Recorder while the real client exits 2, so tests and plans can record calls the real run refuses.
The double Calls() does redundant locking and copying, and the capacity and the iteration may come from different snapshots under concurrent Run. Harmless, but needless.
Nothing in the CLI prints Describe. login --dry-run prints the ssh argv and the gate prints its own preview. The claim "the way --dry-run prints it" (also on Call.Command) is inaccurate.

Validate already renders every role body and the global body (resolving each proxyJump) on a throwaway Client. generateConfig then renders them again, so its two error returns can never fire and each jump is resolved three times.
The doc says it returns what the client was built from, but NoTerminal is dropped. A future Validate check on NoTerminal would silently see false.

A ProxyCommand option on a role with proxyJump is accepted, but ssh silently ignores ProxyCommand after ProxyJump (verified with ssh -G, OpenSSH 9.6). doc/transport.md promises that keywords ssh would ignore are refused.

forwardX11 silently grants trusted X11 forwarding (ForwardX11Trusted yes), which gives the remote host full access to the local display. The field doc and doc/transport.md do not say so, and no test runs this branch.
The bool exists so that Validate can call globalBody(true) without running ssh -V. The literal true at the call site is opaque.

The doc says missing files are skipped so that ssh never reports them, but ssh -G with an Include of a nonexistent file exits 0 without a message (OpenSSH 9.6). The skip only changes the generated file's content.

Any element with two or more colons is accepted as an address. proxyJump 'gw.example.org:22:' passes Validate and is written as 'ProxyJump gw.example.org:22:'. ssh then refuses the whole file ('Invalid ProxyJump ... terminating'), so every connection fails (verified with OpenSSH 9.6).

With role gw {host: 2001:db8::1} and role a {proxyJump: gw}, Validate returns nil and the file gets 'ProxyJump alice@2001:db8::1'. ssh -G then exits 255 with 'Invalid ProxyJump' for any host (verified). HostRole.host and doc/transport.md both allow addresses.

A relative ssh.controlPath passes. ssh resolves it against each process's working directory, so masters are not shared and sockets land wherever clusterctl runs. doc/transport.md says configured paths are absolute.

A second host validator that disagrees with hostname.CheckHost, which destination() uses. Role host 'u_x.example.org' passes Validate and config validate, then every command on the role fails on '_' (verified). Colon strings reach ProxyJump (see parseHop).

The two user-name validators disagree. DefaultUser 'alice@AD.EXAMPLE.ORG' or 'host$' passes Validate, yet destination() refuses it on every command. '.alice' is refused by Validate although destination and the HostRole schema accept it (verified).
allowLines is a mode flag whose name hides that it also allows tab. The literal false at four call sites is opaque.
A verbatim copy of the tilde half of config.ExpandPath. The two copies can drift apart.
A hand-rolled duplicate (another copy lives in internal/output) of slices.Sorted(maps.Keys(m)), available on Go 1.26.
Destination exists only to export destination (L329), which Args calls under the other name. Two names and two doc comments cover one behaviour.

The pid file names an unrelated live process (crash, pid reuse). `tunnel status -o json` then emits {"running":false,"pid":<that pid>} (verified by a probe). The table hides the PID when down, but the object does not, which invites a script to kill the wrong process.
The stated reason is wrong: removeStale does not need the pid. The pid is used only for Stop's error text. That leaves the two-meaning return undocumented, and Status copies it into its output.

The name and doc ('removes a process id file that names no tunnel') suggest it verifies staleness. It deletes whatever file is there, and Stop calls it on a still-live tunnel's file.

The output says 'built <Date>', but .goreleaser.yaml injects {{ .CommitDate }} and the fallback is vcs.time; both are commit timestamps. Info.Date's doc hedges ('build or commit'). Users will read the commit date as the build date.

After one pass over all axes, nothing more ever merges. I folded 300k random 2-4 dimensional sets with mixed padding using one pass and got identical output, and it can be proved for 2-D and 3-D. The repeat pass and foldAxis's bool result do nothing.

target is the same rangeSet as vectors[i].dims[axis], so the function changes its input. The doc does not say so, and it is the reason foldOneAxis has to rebuild unitVectors for every axis. A caller that reused its input would get corrupted vectors.

String is injective on normalised values and pads at every autostep, and 20k random sets gave the same keys with and without autostep. So the parameter only adds cost (it runs arithmeticRun for every key) and forces callers to pass it along.

The doc says it folds progressions of at least n elements and that n=2 enables it. With n=2, exe[1,3] still prints exe[1,3] (ClusterShell 1.10.1 prints exe[1-3/2]), yet exe[1,3,4] prints exe[1-3/2,4]. The cause is the i+2>=len guard in rangeset.go:233.

Most callers write `_ = x.Add(name)` with a single host name, for example bmc.go:843 with fields[0] taken from command output. A name containing , ! & ^ [ or whitespace is then evaluated as an expression, and a malformed one is dropped silently. The doc does not say that groups are rejected.
No test uses a name containing %. Removing the %% unescape here, or the escaping in parsePattern, passes the whole suite, although such names would then print wrongly.

Every host in result was charged to the shared budget, which starts at maxSetElements, so result.Len() can never exceed the cap. The check is dead: removing it passes every test. The limits comment (L18-22) still presents it as a separate mechanism.
No test checks the message. TestParseErrors asserts only err != nil, and the cli test only the substring "operand". Swapping "left" and "right" passes the suite.

Three branches are untested. Dropping the % escaping survives. Ignoring the error of a bare literal over 18 digits survives, and the name would then render as exe0. A budget used up exactly, then a plain name (exe[1-100],exe1 at limit 100), is never reached.

No test depends on normalPad: replacing it with 'return pad' passes the suite. Without it, exe9,exe[08-10] folds to exe[08,9,10], which re-parses and prints as exe[08,9-10]. That breaks the fold idempotence the package promises.

exe[1-] parses as exe1, and exe[1-,5] as exe[1,5]; ClusterShell 1.10.1 rejects both. So exe[1-$N] with an empty substitution silently selects exe1. This is the empty-substitution case the package deliberately rejects for dangling operators.
The doc does not mention the 18-digit cap, which is the overflow guard for expandSpans. A 19-digit host number fails with a bare 'invalid number' and no mention of length.
Because of the parameter, %v on a *rangeSet ignores this method, and the name reads inconsistently next to vector.render(autostep), which does the same job one level up.

With WithAutostep(2), exe[1,3] prints exe[1,3] but exe[1,3,10] prints exe[1-3/2,10] (verified). The i+2>=len guard skips a two-element run at the tail, but a two-element run found mid-set is returned. This contradicts its own doc (longest run) and WithAutostep's 'at least n elements'. The output still round-trips, so the harm is cosmetic.
Every test that builds one expects an error (@missing, @other:compute, the cycle, the limits), so setting Default to "" still passes the suite.

Evaluation is strictly left to right, so an operator inside one group applies to everything before it. With a=exe2 and b=exe[1-4]!exe2, @a,@b is exe[1-4] but @* is exe[1,3-4]. internal/groups.Resolver.All repeats this pattern.
No test executes it, and nothing in the repository calls Resolver.DefaultSource through the interface.
